proposal.root_cause: Repair turn is triggered only by errors/zero rows and its guidance is a fixed literal-matching checklist, so (a) cleanly-executing but semantically wrong drafts are never re-examined and (b) empty-result repairs get no column-level evidence about WHERE the mentioned value actually lives
proposal.what: Rework solve.py's second call: probe every text column for question-quoted phrases AND distinctive question words (reporting exact hits with counts vs. substring-only hits), attach an FK join map plus small distinct-value samples of short low-cardinality text columns referenced by the draft, show the draft's first result rows, and trigger the repair on execution error, zero rows, or a static alias-shadowing check on correlated subqueries; replace the fixed checklist with neutral, evidence-driven diagnostic instructions. Also soften the projection rule in system_prompt.md from a blanket 'select all columns' to 'unspecified attributes -> that entity's own table columns', since a bare 'Which X ...' identification question does not ask for unspecified attributes.

edits.system_prompt.md:
You are an expert SQLite analyst. Given a database schema and a question, write one SQLite query that answers the question.
Return the query in a single ```sql code block.

Rules:
- Select exactly what the question asks for — no extra columns, no missing ones, in the order asked.
  * If specific attributes are named ("first, middle and last name", "ids", "how many"), select exactly those.
  * If the question asks for "details", "all information", or otherwise unspecified attributes of an entity ("What are the details for ...", "Show the paragraphs that ..."), select all columns of that entity's own table (T1.*), not just its name and not the columns of tables joined only for filtering.
  * A bare identification question ("Which countries have ...", "List the students who ...") asks for the entity itself: select that entity's table columns.
- Match string values to how they are actually stored. Questions often quote text loosely: prefer case-insensitive substring matching (LOWER(col) LIKE '%keyword%') for phrases embedded in longer text, and keep any trailing spaces shown in the question when matching. Filter on the column that truly holds the value (the text/description column that contains it, not a code or a similarly named column of another table).
- Never use NOT IN with a subquery whose column may contain NULL (it silently returns nothing); use NOT EXISTS or filter out NULLs. In a correlated subquery, alias the outer table and reference that alias explicitly so the inner reference cannot resolve to the inner table. For "has no X" questions over a relation table, check both sides of the relation.
- Join through the declared foreign keys; do not invent join conditions.
- Use DISTINCT when duplicates would otherwise appear; use ORDER BY + LIMIT for superlatives/"top" questions; handle ties only when asked.
- Follow the hint/evidence exactly when provided (formulas, value mappings, column choices).
- Return only the final query in one ```sql block.

  task  {"id", "db_id", "question", "hint"}      (hint is BIRD's evidence; "" for Spider)
  env.chat(messages, max_tokens=None) -> str     policy call (capped per task: env.max_calls)
  env.schema(db_id) -> str                       CREATE statements of the database
  env.execute(sql, max_rows=20) -> dict          read-only run: {ok, columns, rows, n_rows, error}
  env.descriptions(db_id) -> str                 column descriptions if the dataset ships them, else ""
  env.prompt(name) -> str                        text of a file in this harness
  env.config -> dict                             parsed config.json
"""

import re

SQL_BLOCK = re.compile(r"```(?:sql|sqlite)?\s*(.*?)```", re.S | re.I)
LITERAL = re.compile(r"'((?:[^']|'')*)'")
QUOTED = re.compile(r"[\"'\u2018\u2019\u201c\u201d]([^\"'\u2018\u2019\u201c\u201d]{2,60})[\"'\u2018\u2019\u201c\u201d]")
CREATE_RE = re.compile(
    r"CREATE\s+TABLE\s+(?:IF\s+NOT\s+EXISTS\s+)?[`\[\"]?([\w ]+?)[`\]\"]?\s*\((.*)\)\s*;",
    re.S | re.I,
)
TEXTY = re.compile(r"CHAR|CLOB|TEXT|STRING|VARCHAR", re.I)
NUMERIC = re.compile(r"INT|REAL|FLOA|DOUB|DEC|NUM|BOOL|DATE|TIME", re.I)
STOP = set(
    """a an the of for and or to in on at by with from as is are was were be been being do does did
    have has had not no nor than then that this these those there here it its their them they he she
    his her him we you your our us i me my mine what which who whom whose when where why how many
    much most more least less all any both each every some such other others another same only own
    too very can could will would shall should may might must list show find give tell name names
    id ids number count total average sum maximum minimum highest lowest largest smallest greatest
    top first last next please return display report also between among across per via using use
    value values row rows record records data information detail details everything everybody
    everyone anybody anyone somebody someone something thing things people person student students
    year years month months day days time times date dates make made get got want need like
    different distinct order ordered sort sorted limit result results answer question following
    true false yes none null empty full one two three four five six seven eight nine ten
    """.split()
)


def extract_sql(text):
    blocks = [b.strip() for b in SQL_BLOCK.findall(text or "") if b.strip()]
    if blocks:
        return blocks[-1].rstrip(";").strip()
    return (text or "").strip().rstrip(";").strip()


def _split_top(body):
    parts, depth, cur, quote = [], 0, "", None
    for ch in body:
        if quote:
            cur += ch
            if ch == quote:
                quote = None
            continue
        if ch in "'\"`":
            quote = ch
            cur += ch
            continue
        if ch == "(":
            depth += 1
        elif ch == ")":
            depth -= 1
        if ch == "," and depth == 0:
            parts.append(cur)
            cur = ""
        else:
            cur += ch
    parts.append(cur)
    return parts


def _parse_schema(schema):
    """tables: name -> [(col, type)]; fks: list of (table, col, ref_table, ref_col)."""
    tables, fks = {}, []
    for m in CREATE_RE.finditer(schema or ""):
        name, body = m.group(1).strip(), m.group(2)
        cols = []
        for p in _split_top(body):
            p = p.strip()
            if not p:
                continue
            up = p.upper()
            fm = re.match(
                r"(?:CONSTRAINT\s+[`\[\"]?[\w ]+[`\]\"]?\s+)?FOREIGN\s+KEY\s*\(\s*[`\[\"]?([\w ]+?)[`\]\"]?\s*\)"
                r"\s*REFERENCES\s+[`\[\"]?([\w ]+?)[`\]\"]?\s*(?:\(\s*[`\[\"]?([\w ]+?)[`\]\"]?\s*\))?",
                p,
                re.I,
            )
            if fm:
                fks.append((name, fm.group(1).strip(), fm.group(2).strip(),
                            (fm.group(3) or "").strip()))
                continue
            if up.startswith(("PRIMARY", "UNIQUE", "CHECK", "CONSTRAINT", "KEY", "FOREIGN")):
                continue
            cm = re.match(r"[`\[\"]?([\w ]+?)[`\]\"]?\s*(.*)$", p, re.S)
            if cm:
                cols.append((cm.group(1).strip(), cm.group(2).strip()))
        tables[name] = cols
    return tables, fks


def _is_text(typ):
    t = typ or ""
    if TEXTY.search(t):
        return True
    head = re.split(r"[\s(]", t.strip(), 1)[0]
    return not NUMERIC.search(head)


def _esc(s):
    return s.replace("'", "''")


def _run(env, sql, max_rows=5):
    try:
        r = env.execute(sql, max_rows=max_rows)
    except Exception:
        return None
    if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("ok"):
        return r
    return None


def _keywords(question, hint):
    kws = []
    for m in QUOTED.finditer(question or ""):
        v = m.group(1).strip()
        if len(v) >= 2 and v not in kws:
            kws.append(v)
    words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z\-']{2,}", (question or "") + " " + (hint or ""))
    words = [w for w in words if w.lower() not in STOP]
    words.sort(key=len, reverse=True)
    for w in words:
        if w not in kws:
            kws.append(w)
    return kws[:6]


def _probe_values(env, tables, sql, question, hint):
    """Locate where the values mentioned in the question actually live."""
    keys = _keywords(question, hint)
    lits = []
    for m in LITERAL.finditer(sql or ""):
        v = m.group(1).replace("''", "'").strip()
        if len(v) >= 2 and v not in keys:
            keys.append(v)
        if len(v) >= 2:
            lits.append(v.lower())
    if not keys:
        return ""
    text_cols = [(t, c) for t, cols in tables.items() for c, ty in cols if _is_text(ty)]
    notes, budget = [], 14
    for key in keys[:5]:
        core = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9 ]", " ", key).split()
        token = max(core, key=len) if core else key
        token = token[:24].lower()
        if len(token) < 3:
            continue
        exact_hits, like_hits = [], []
        for t, c in text_cols:
            if budget <= 0:
                break
            q = (f'SELECT DISTINCT "{c}" FROM "{t}" '
                 f"WHERE LOWER(\"{c}\") LIKE '%{_esc(token)}%' LIMIT 4")
            r = _run(env, q, 4)
            budget -= 1
            if not r or not r.get("rows"):
                continue
            vals = [str(row[0]) for row in r["rows"]]
            exact = [v for v in vals if v.strip().lower() == key.strip().lower()]
            if exact:
                exact_hits.append(f"{t}.{c} = {exact}")
            else:
                like_hits.append(f"{t}.{c}: {vals}")
        if exact_hits:
            notes.append(f"'{key}' is stored EXACTLY in " + "; ".join(exact_hits[:3]))
        elif like_hits:
            notes.append(f"'{key}' has NO exact match anywhere; substring hits -> "
                         + "; ".join(like_hits[:3]))
        if len(notes) >= 4:
            break
    # Small categorical columns used by the draft: show the real value vocabulary.
    used = set(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_]\w*", sql or ""))
    shown, cbudget = [], 4
    for t, cols in tables.items():
        if t.lower() not in {u.lower() for u in used}:
            continue
        for c, ty in cols:
            if cbudget <= 0 or len(shown) >= 3:
                break
            if not _is_text(ty) or c.lower() not in {u.lower() for u in used}:
                continue
            if any(c.lower() == lit or lit in c.lower() for lit in lits):
                continue
            r = _run(env, f'SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT "{c}") FROM "{t}"', 1)
            if not r or not r.get("rows"):
                cbudget -= 1
                continue
            try:
                n = int(r["rows"][0][0])
            except Exception:
                continue
            if not (1 < n <= 12):
                continue
            r2 = _run(env, f'SELECT DISTINCT "{c}" FROM "{t}" LIMIT 12', 12)
            cbudget -= 1
            if r2 and r2.get("rows"):
                vals = [str(x[0]) for x in r2["rows"]]
                shown.append(f"{t}.{c} possible values: {vals}")
    if shown:
        notes.append("\n".join(shown))
    return "\n".join(notes)[:1800]


def _fk_map(tables, fks, sql):
    used = {u.lower() for u in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_]\w*", sql or "")}
    lines = []
    for t, c, rt, rc in fks:
        if t.lower() in used or rt.lower() in used:
            lines.append(f"{t}.{c} -> {rt}.{rc or '(primary key)'}")
    return "\n".join(lines[:12])


def _shadow_note(sql, tables):
    """Flag correlated subqueries whose bare column resolves to the inner table."""
    if not sql or not re.search(r"\bEXISTS\b|\bIN\s*\(", sql, re.I):
        return ""
    lower = sql.lower()
    issues = []
    for m in re.finditer(r"\(\s*SELECT\b", sql, re.I):
        start = m.start()
        depth, end = 0, len(sql)
        for i in range(start, len(sql)):
            if sql[i] == "(":
                depth += 1
            elif sql[i] == ")":
                depth -= 1
                if depth == 0:
                    end = i
                    break
        inner = sql[start + 1:end]
        outer = sql[:start] + sql[end:]
        inner_tabs = re.findall(r"\b(?:FROM|JOIN)\s+[`\[\"]?(\w+)", inner, re.I)
        outer_tabs = re.findall(r"\b(?:FROM|JOIN)\s+[`\[\"]?(\w+)", outer, re.I)
        inner_cols = set()
        for t in inner_tabs:
            for name, cols in tables.items():
                if name.lower() == t.lower():
                    inner_cols |= {c.lower() for c, _ in cols}
        for om in re.finditer(r"\b(\w+)\.(\w+)\b", inner):
            alias, col = om.group(1), om.group(2)
            if col.lower() not in inner_cols:
                continue
            resolves_outer = any(a.lower() == alias.lower() for a in outer_tabs)
            resolves_inner = any(a.lower() == alias.lower() for a in inner_tabs)
            if resolves_outer and not resolves_inner:
                continue
            if not resolves_outer:
                issues.append(
                    f"'{alias}.{col}' inside the subquery does not refer to any table listed in the "
                    f"outer query's FROM/JOIN; the correlation may be broken."
                )
            elif resolves_inner:
                issues.append(
                    f"'{alias}.{col}' inside the subquery resolves to the subquery's own table, so the "
                    f"subquery is not correlated with the outer row."
                )
        if issues:
            break
    if not issues:
        return ""
    return ("STATIC CHECK: " + " ".join(issues[:2]) +
            " Rewrite the correlation explicitly (alias the outer table and reference that alias, "
            "or use a LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL / EXCEPT formulation) and make sure the predicate really "
            "depends on the outer row.")


def _result_note(res):
    if not res.get("ok"):
        return f"ERROR: {res.get('error')}"
    if res.get("n_rows", 0) == 0:
        return "The query executed but returned ZERO rows."
    return None


def solve(task, env):
    schema = env.schema(task["db_id"])
    user = f"Database: {task['db_id']}\n\nSchema:\n{schema}\n\nQuestion: {task['question']}"
    if task.get("hint"):
        user += f"\nHint: {task['hint']}"
    try:
        desc = env.descriptions(task["db_id"]) or ""
    except Exception:
        desc = ""
    if desc.strip():
        user += f"\n\nColumn descriptions:\n{desc.strip()[:2000]}"

    messages = [
        {"role": "system", "content": env.prompt("system_prompt.md")},
        {"role": "user", "content": user},
    ]
    reply = env.chat(messages, max_tokens=env.config.get("max_tokens", 800))
    sql = extract_sql(reply)

    try:
        res = env.execute(sql, max_rows=20)
    except Exception as e:
        res = {"ok": False, "error": str(e), "rows": [], "n_rows": 0}

    try:
        tables, fks = _parse_schema(schema)
    except Exception:
        tables, fks = {}, []

    note = _result_note(res)
    shadow = ""
    try:
        shadow = _shadow_note(sql, tables)
    except Exception:
        shadow = ""
    if note is None and not shadow:
        return {"sql": sql}

    evidence = ""
    try:
        evidence = _probe_values(env, tables, sql, task["question"], task.get("hint", ""))
    except Exception:
        evidence = ""
    fkmap = ""
    try:
        fkmap = _fk_map(tables, fks, sql)
    except Exception:
        fkmap = ""

    repair = f"Your draft query:\n```sql\n{sql}\n```\n"
    if note:
        repair += note + "\n"
    else:
        repair += "It executed and returned rows, but a static check found a possible logic bug.\n"
        if res.get("rows"):
            repair += f"First rows returned: {res['rows'][:3]}\n"
    if shadow:
        repair += "\n" + shadow + "\n"
    if evidence:
        repair += f"\nEvidence probed from the actual database:\n{evidence}\n"
    if fkmap:
        repair += f"\nDeclared foreign keys (use these join paths):\n{fkmap}\n"
    repair += (
        "\nRe-read the question and the schema, then decide what is actually wrong before rewriting. "
        "Use the evidence above rather than guessing:\n"
        "- If a quoted phrase or keyword was found in a DIFFERENT table/column than the one you "
        "filtered, filter that column instead. If it exists exactly somewhere, prefer equality on "
        "that column over a loose LIKE on another one; if it only appears as a substring, match the "
        "substring (and preserve any trailing space the question shows).\n"
        "- If a value is absent everywhere, the concept is probably encoded differently (another "
        "column, a code, a category label, or a derived expression given in the hint).\n"
        "- Check the join path against the declared foreign keys; a missing or wrong join silently "
        "drops or duplicates rows.\n"
        "- For negation ('no X', 'never', 'not'), make sure the subquery is genuinely correlated with "
        "the outer row and that every side of a relation is considered; NOT IN over a nullable column "
        "returns nothing.\n"
        "- Re-check the projection: return exactly the attributes asked for, in the asked order.\n"
        "If after this analysis the draft is in fact correct, return it unchanged. Otherwise return "
        "ONLY the corrected query in a single ```sql block."
    )
    messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply})
    messages.append({"role": "user", "content": repair})
    try:
        reply2 = env.chat(messages, max_tokens=env.config.get("max_tokens", 800))
    except Exception:
        return {"sql": sql}
    sql2 = extract_sql(reply2)
    if not sql2:
        return {"sql": sql}
    try:
        res2 = env.execute(sql2, max_rows=20)
    except Exception:
        res2 = {"ok": False}
    if res2.get("ok"):
        return {"sql": sql2}
    return {"sql": sql}

You are an expert SQLite analyst. Given a database schema and a question, write one SQLite query that answers the question.
Return the query in a single ```sql code block.

Rules:
- Select exactly what the question asks for — no extra columns, no missing ones, in the order asked.
  * If specific attributes are named ("first, middle and last name", "ids", "how many"), select exactly those.
  * If the question asks for "details", "all information", or otherwise unspecified attributes of an entity ("What are the details for ...", "Show the paragraphs that ..."), select all columns of that entity's own table (T1.*), not just its name and not the columns of tables joined only for filtering.
  * A bare identification question ("Which countries have ...", "List the students who ...") asks for the entity itself: select that entity's table columns.
- Match string values to how they are actually stored. Questions often quote text loosely: prefer case-insensitive substring matching (LOWER(col) LIKE '%keyword%') for phrases embedded in longer text, and keep any trailing spaces shown in the question when matching. Filter on the column that truly holds the value (the text/description column that contains it, not a code or a similarly named column of another table).
- Never use NOT IN with a subquery whose column may contain NULL (it silently returns nothing); use NOT EXISTS or filter out NULLs. In a correlated subquery, alias the outer table and reference that alias explicitly so the inner reference cannot resolve to the inner table. For "has no X" questions over a relation table, check both sides of the relation.
- Join through the declared foreign keys; do not invent join conditions.
- Use DISTINCT when duplicates would otherwise appear; use ORDER BY + LIMIT for superlatives/"top" questions; handle ties only when asked.
- Follow the hint/evidence exactly when provided (formulas, value mappings, column choices).
- Return only the final query in one ```sql block.
